body.x: ET Manufacturing, an Indian manufacturing industry outlet, named BRATO, D,RIVE and AeiROBOT its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

ET Manufacturing is a manufacturing industry platform run by The Economic Times, the business daily of the Times Group, a leading Indian business media group. It covers the manufacturing value chain, including automotive and electric vehicles, electronics and semiconductors, robotics and automation, and process industries, and its main readers are industry decision-makers such as corporate executives and manufacturing and technology heads.

Deepanshu Taumar, deputy editor at ET Auto, was invited to FIX 2024 as a global media representative. This year, Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor at The Economic Times - Business Vertical, was invited as the representative of ET Manufacturing.

The three companies selected for BEST OF FIX 2026 work on technologies tied to automation and efficiency gains at industrial sites: precision reducers, vehicle data-based fleet monitoring and a humanoid robot.
BRATO Supplies High-Rigidity Planetary Reducers for Robots and Automation

BRATO, led by its CEO, manufactures precision planetary reducers for servo motors. Its flagship BP Series is designed to connect directly to a servo motor, and its high precision and rigidity suit fields that need precise control and high-torque transmission. Main applications include industrial and transfer robots, machine tools, automation equipment, display manufacturing equipment and shipbuilding components.

A reducer is a core component that adjusts a motor's rotation speed and torque so that robot joints and automation equipment move precisely. As manufacturing sites automate further and demand for precise robot work grows, the quality, durability and control performance of reducers matter more. BRATO supplies products built on a low-backlash design and a planetary gear structure, aiming for high efficiency, low noise and durability, and contributes to domestic production of precision drive components and stronger manufacturing capability.
D,RIVE Monitors Fleets in Real Time With Vehicle ECU Data

D,RIVE, led by its CEO, is a mobility data company that supports vehicle operation and driving management using data collected directly from vehicles' electronic control units (ECUs). Going beyond vehicle tracking centered on GPS location, it collects and analyzes ECU data such as speed, engine revolutions per minute (RPM) and vehicle condition in real time to track driving status and manage drivers' habits and fleet efficiency.

D,RIVE's fleet management system (FMS) offers real-time vehicle monitoring, driving history analysis, vehicle maintenance and trip scheduling and dispatch management on one platform. According to the company's official website, it can collect 221 data items per vehicle, and it reports 75 million cumulative ECU data records and operating results from more than 400 monitored vehicles. The company is also using the data accumulated in vehicle operation to expand into maintenance and cost management, dispatch optimization, autonomous driving training data and mobility AI development.

Vehicle operating data can underpin safety and cost efficiency in logistics and delivery, school and commuter transport, passenger transport and corporate fleets. By using ECU data directly for monitoring, D,RIVE drew attention as a company helping businesses run their fleets on data and making mobility services more efficient.
AeiROBOT Develops the ALICE Humanoid for Manufacturing and Industrial Automation

AeiROBOT, a humanoid robot company led by its CEO, develops robot platforms that reproduce human movement and ways of working. Its work spans hardware and software, including the ALICE series of humanoid robots, actuators that drive the robots, walking control and AI-based autonomous systems.

AeiROBOT is aiming for a multipurpose robot platform that can replace people or work alongside them, and is widening its possible uses at industrial sites such as manufacturing, shipbuilding and construction. Using its own actuation technology and robot control capability, it is refining humanoid technology that can perform a range of motions to suit the work environment, and is looking for robot solutions that can address labor shortages and dangerous work at industrial sites.

Humanoid robots draw attention as a new option for manufacturing automation because they can work in a human-like way within existing workspaces and with existing tools. By applying its robot platform at industrial sites and improving AI-based autonomous work capability, AeiROBOT is pointing to what manufacturing automation could look like in the physical AI era.
Where Precision Parts, Data and Robots Meet Production

ET Manufacturing's top three span different technology fields that support productivity and automation in manufacturing. BRATO's precision reducers support the exact drive of robots and automation equipment, D,RIVE's vehicle data-based monitoring helps make mobility operations such as transport and logistics more efficient, and AeiROBOT's humanoid technology points toward industrial environments where people and robots work together.

ET Manufacturing noted that a major recent change in manufacturing is AI moving beyond pilot projects into actual production. It sees companies moving to extend AI to quality inspection, predictive maintenance, energy management and production planning, while electrification, vehicle software, robotics and automation technology emerge as factors that decide manufacturers' competitiveness.

The selection gave Korean companies' manufacturing, mobility and robot technologies a look through the eyes of an international industry outlet and widened their contact with overseas markets. ET Manufacturing's focus on the manufacturing value chain and industrial automation gives the selection added weight as a judgment of a technology's practicality and use at industrial sites.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including ET Manufacturing. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report on innovative Korean companies in future industries to audiences around the world.
